title: Tor of an opcycle cokernel is detected by preceding tensor homology
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, viewed as the structure ring on the one-point site. Let P^\bullet be a cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are flat A-modules [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let a be an integer, and put Q = P^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1}). For every A-module N there is a natural A-linear surjection H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_A N) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] \twoheadrightarrow \operatorname{Tor}_1^A(Q,N) [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653), Tor_1 argument in the proof

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})\subseteq P^a$ and write $d^{a-1}$ as a surjection $\pi:P^{a-1}\to K$ followed by the inclusion $\iota:K\hookrightarrow P^a$. The low-degree Tor sequence [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] for $0\to K\xrightarrow{\iota}P^a\to Q\to0$ gives an exact segment $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(P^a,N)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(Q,N)\xrightarrow{\delta_N}K\otimes_AN\xrightarrow{\iota\otimes1}P^a\otimes_AN$, with $\delta$ natural in $N$. Next, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(P^a,N)=0$: by [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] it is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(N,P^a)$, the first homology of $F_\bullet\otimes_AP^a$ for a free resolution $F_\bullet\to N$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. With $Z=\operatorname{im}(F_1\to F_0)$, the sequence $F_2\otimes_AP^a\to F_1\otimes_AP^a\to Z\otimes_AP^a\to0$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], and $Z\otimes_AP^a\to F_0\otimes_AP^a$ is injective because $P^a$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; hence $\ker(F_1\otimes_AP^a\to F_0\otimes_AP^a)=\operatorname{im}(F_2\otimes_AP^a)$. Thus $\delta_N$ identifies $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(Q,N)$, naturally in $N$, with $\ker(\iota\otimes1:K\otimes_AN\to P^a\otimes_AN)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653), Tor_1 argument in the proof

proof.text: Regard $N$ as a complex in degree $0$; then the degree-$(a-1)$ differential of $P^\bullet\otimes_AN$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is $d^{a-1}\otimes1=(\iota\otimes1)\circ(\pi\otimes1)$, and $\pi\otimes1:P^{a-1}\otimes_AN\to K\otimes_AN$ is surjective by right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. Let $Z^{a-1}=\ker(d^{a-1}\otimes1)$, so $H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_AN)=Z^{a-1}/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-2}\otimes1)$ [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. For $x\in Z^{a-1}$ one has $(\iota\otimes1)(\pi\otimes1)(x)=0$, so $\pi\otimes1$ maps $Z^{a-1}$ into $\ker(\iota\otimes1)$; and $(\pi\otimes1)\circ(d^{a-2}\otimes1)=(\pi\circ d^{a-2})\otimes1=0$ because $\iota\circ\pi\circ d^{a-2}=d^{a-1}d^{a-2}=0$ and $\iota$ is injective. Hence $\pi\otimes1$ induces an $A$-linear map $\bar\pi_N:H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_AN)\to\ker(\iota\otimes1)$, natural in $N$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653), Tor_1 argument in the proof

proof.text: $\bar\pi_N$ is surjective: let $y\in K\otimes_AN$ with $(\iota\otimes1)(y)=0$. By the surjectivity of $\pi\otimes1$ from Step 2 choose $x\in P^{a-1}\otimes_AN$ with $(\pi\otimes1)(x)=y$. Then $(d^{a-1}\otimes1)(x)=(\iota\otimes1)(y)=0$, so $x\in Z^{a-1}$ and $\bar\pi_N[x]=y$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653), Tor_1 argument in the proof

proof.text: The composite $\delta_N^{-1}\circ\bar\pi_N:H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_AN)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(Q,N)$ of the surjection of Steps 2--3 with the inverse of the isomorphism $\delta_N$ onto $\ker(\iota\otimes1)$ of Step 1 is an $A$-linear surjection. For $g:N\to N'$ both $\bar\pi$ (induced by $\pi\otimes1$) and $\delta$ (by the naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable], with Tor functorial as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]) commute with the maps induced by $g$, so the surjection is natural in $N$.

split_report.summary: Split the Tag 0653 Tor argument directly. The short exact sequence for the opcycle cokernel and the low-degree Tor sequence identify Tor_1(Q,N) with a kernel because P^a is flat; tensor right exactness and the differential identify that kernel as a quotient of preceding tensor homology, with naturality inherited from the constructions.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Tor_1 argument in the ancestor's Tag 0654 truncation proof: the degree-a opcycle cokernel is controlled by the preceding tensor homology.

tool_uses.why: The low-degree long exact Tor sequence is the generic homological tool used to identify Tor_1 of the cokernel with a tensor kernel.
Right exactness supplies lifts from P^{a-1} tensor N to the image module tensor N; the Picard unit has no replacement for this module fact.
Tor symmetry reduces Tor_1(P^a,N)=0 for flat P^a to exactness of a free resolution of N tensored with P^a; a generic module fact.
